Udhampur News: भूस्खलन से रास्ता बंद, घरों पर भी खतरा
विज्ञापन
उधमपुर। ब्लॉक घोरडी की पंचायत हरतयान के वार्ड नंबर दो के लरदागा-लेहड़ी गांव के लोगों ने रास्ते की मांग को लेकर रविवार को प्रदर्शन किया। ग्रामीणों ने कहा कि हाल ही में हुई बारिश के दौरान हुए भूस्खलन से गांव का रास्ता पूरी तरह कट गया है। इससे लोगों की आवाजाही प्रभावित हो गई है, वहीं भूस्खलन वाले हिस्से के आसपास बने मकानों पर भी गिरने का खतरा मंडरा रहा है।
प्रदर्शन की अगुवाई कर रहे स्थानीय समाजसेवक एवं स्किल डेवलपमेंट फॉर विलेज काउंसिल के अध्यक्ष डॉ. अवि कुमार ने कहा कि वार्ड नंबर दो का यह रास्ता सलमाटा, लरदागा, लेहड़ी और बरमीन गांवों के लोगों के लिए काफी महत्वपूर्ण है और आसपास के इलाकों के लिए यह शॉर्टकट के रूप में इस्तेमाल होता है। रास्ता कट जाने के कारण इन गांवों के लोगों को आने-जाने में परेशानी का सामना करना पड़ रहा है।
उन्होंने कहा कि रास्ता कटने के बाद भी संबंधित क्षेत्र में भूस्खलन का खतरा बना हुआ है। प्रभावित हिस्से के ठीक ऊपरी क्षेत्र में बने मकानों के लिए भी खतरा पैदा हो गया है। ऐसे में प्रशासन को जल्द रास्ते की मरम्मत करवाने के साथ-साथ भूस्खलन प्रभावित हिस्से में क्रेट अथवा सुरक्षा दीवार का निर्माण करवाना चाहिए ताकि लोगों के घरों और जान-माल की सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित हो सके।
विज्ञापन
ग्रामीणों ने चिनैनी-घोरड़ी विधानसभा क्षेत्र के विधायक और प्रशासन से जल्द समस्या का समाधान करवाने की मांग की। प्रदर्शनकारियों ने चेतावनी दी कि यदि जल्द उनकी मांगों पर कार्रवाई नहीं हुई तो वे आंदोलन को और तेज करने के लिए मजबूर होंगे। जरूरत पड़ने पर प्रशासन का पुतला जलाकर भी विरोध जताने की चेतावनी दी गई।

articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir Assembly में जबरदस्त हंगामा, विधानसभा अध्यक्ष भी बोले पड़े, 'गुंडागर्दी नहीं चलेगी' - Prabhasakshi

By नीरज कुमार दुबे | Sep 21, 2026
जम्मू-कश्मीर विधानसभा का शरद सत्र शुरू होते ही सदन सियासी टकराव का अखाड़ा बन गया। पहले ही दिन भारतीय जनता पार्टी के विधायकों ने सरकार को घेरते हुए जोरदार नारेबाजी की, सदन के बीचोंबीच पहुंचकर विरोध जताया और रोजगार, बिजली, दैनिक वेतनभोगियों तथा स्वास्थ्य मिशन से जुड़े कर्मचारियों के मुद्दे उठाए। जवाब में सत्तापक्ष ने जम्मू-कश्मीर के पूर्ण राज्य के दर्जे की बहाली का मुद्दा उछाल दिया। शोर-शराबा इतना बढ़ा कि विधानसभा अध्यक्ष अब्दुल रहीम राठेर को कड़ी चेतावनी देनी पड़ी, “गुंडागर्दी नहीं चलेगी।”
इसे भी पढ़ें: Manoj Sinha ने SMVDSB बैठक में कटरा के International Museum of Goddess की समीक्षा की
भाजपा के इस विरोध के बीच सत्ता पक्ष ने भी मोर्चा संभाल लिया। नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस, कांग्रेस और मार्क्सवादी कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी के विधायकों ने जम्मू-कश्मीर का पूर्ण राज्य का दर्जा बहाल करने की मांग को लेकर नारे लगाए। मार्क्सवादी कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी के विधायक एम.वाई. तारिगामी ने कहा कि दो वर्ष बीत चुके हैं, लेकिन राज्य का दर्जा बहाल करने का वादा अब तक पूरा नहीं हुआ है। सत्ता पक्ष का तर्क रहा कि राज्य का दर्जा बहाल होना जम्मू-कश्मीर की राजनीतिक और संवैधानिक स्थिति से जुड़ा प्रमुख सवाल है।
हंगामे के बीच कांग्रेस विधायकों ने भी केंद्र के खिलाफ नारेबाजी की। सदन में एक तरफ उमर सरकार से रोजगार और जनसुविधाओं पर जवाब मांगा जा रहा था तो दूसरी तरफ राज्य का दर्जा बहाल करने की मांग गूंज रही थी। नतीजा यह हुआ कि प्रश्नकाल गंभीर बहस की बजाय नारेबाजी में उलझ गया और कार्यवाही बाधित होती रही।
उपमुख्यमंत्री सुरिंदर चौधरी ने विपक्ष पर सदन की कार्यवाही बाधित करने का आरोप लगाते हुए कहा कि सरकार सभी सवालों का जवाब देने के लिए तैयार है, लेकिन विपक्ष को मुद्दे एक-एक करके उठाने चाहिए। दूसरी ओर नेता प्रतिपक्ष सुनील शर्मा ने आरोप लगाया कि उमर अब्दुल्ला सरकार जनता से जुड़े सवालों से बचने की कोशिश कर रही है। उनका कहना है कि बेरोजगार युवाओं, आउटसोर्स कर्मचारियों और दैनिक वेतनभोगियों की समस्याओं पर सरकार को स्पष्ट जवाब देना चाहिए।
वहीं मुख्यमंत्री उमर अब्दुल्ला ने सत्र को जनता की समस्याओं, आकांक्षाओं और कल्याण से जुड़े मुद्दों पर सार्थक चर्चा का अवसर बताया। लेकिन पहले ही दिन के घटनाक्रम ने साफ कर दिया कि आने वाले दिनों में सरकार और विपक्ष के बीच टकराव तेज रह सकता है। रोजगार, बिजली, आरक्षण, आउटसोर्सिंग, कर्मचारियों का नियमितीकरण और राज्य का दर्जा, ये मुद्दे सदन की कार्यवाही की दिशा तय करने वाले हैं। हालांकि पहले ही दिन जिस तरह हंगामे के बीच सदन को दिनभर के लिए स्थगित करना पड़ा जिससे संकेत मिल रहा है कि सत्र के आने वाले दिन भी हंगामेदार रहने वाले हैं।

articles.title: Jammu Kashmir Govt Examining Extension of Power Amnesty Scheme - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: The Jammu and Kashmir Government is examining an extension of the Power Amnesty Scheme to provide relief to domestic electricity consumers who have been unable to clear their outstanding dues within the stipulated period, the Power Development Department has informed the Legislative Assembly.
The department said a substantial portion of outstanding dues had been recovered from domestic consumers, including those belonging to weaker sections, under the scheme.
Replying to a starred question by Reasi MLA Kuldeep Raj Dubey, the government said the proposed extension of the amnesty scheme was currently being examined “on merits”.
The question had sought details on whether consumers who had paid a substantial part of their dues but could not meet the remaining instalments because of financial constraints would be given relief through a reduction or waiver of subsequently accrued surcharge or interest, or an extension of the repayment period.
On relief for small businesses, shopkeepers and other commercial consumers whose electricity connections had been disconnected despite part-payment of outstanding dues, the department said DISCOMs were facilitating payment of long-pending arrears through instalments.
The government said connections were restored once consumers began clearing their outstanding dues in instalments, subject to an undertaking that the remaining amount would also be paid through mutually agreed instalments.
The department said the arrangement was aimed at facilitating recovery of outstanding revenue while allowing consumers to liquidate their arrears through instalment payments.

articles.title: 200 Units Free Power Scheme for Eligible Jammu Kashmir Households Reaches Final Tender Stage: Govt - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: The Jammu and Kashmir Government has said a scheme to provide 200 units of free electricity to eligible domestic consumers through 2-kW rooftop solar systems is at the final tendering stage, while ruling out any proposal to waive existing electricity arrears after smart metering.
The Power Development Department (PDD) disclosed the position in a written reply to a starred question by MLA Surjit Singh Slathia (Samba) in the J&K Legislative Assembly.
The department said bids for the rooftop solar scheme under the RESCO mode had been opened and were currently under evaluation. Implementation will begin after completion of the prescribed tendering and related formalities.
On smart metering in Samba district, the government said 26,013 of the targeted 36,736 connections had been covered in the Samba constituency. In Vijaypur, 33,106 of 46,308 targeted connections had been completed, while Ramgarh recorded 9,414 against a physical target of 15,739.
The department said financial targets and achievements were not maintained separately for individual constituencies or districts because the smart metering projects were awarded as composite contracts.
Under PMDP Phase-II, Lot-A, the smart metering project covers Samba, Jammu and Udhampur districts. The project has an awarded cost of Rs 338.75 crore, against which financial achievement stands at Rs 314.58 crore.
The smart metering project under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) covers all 10 districts of Jammu Province and has an awarded cost of Rs 983.04 crore. Financial achievement under the project was reported at Rs 34.72 crore.
The department clarified that these financial figures are at project level and cannot be apportioned constituency-wise or district-wise because of the composite nature of the contracts.
On electricity arrears, the government said no proposal is under consideration to waive the dues of consumers following completion of the smart metering process in Samba district.

articles.title: Jammu Kashmir Govt Plans Water Supply Augmentation in Batamaloo, AloochiBagh - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: The Jammu and Kashmir Government has undertaken a series of measures to improve drinking water supply in Batamaloo, AloochiBagh and adjoining densely populated areas of Srinagar, including new overhead tanks, upgraded pumping capacity and additional water treatment facilities.
The measures were detailed in the government’s reply to a starred question by Lal Chowk MLA Sheikh Ahsan Ahmed Pardesi regarding the reported scarcity of potable water in S.D. Colony Batamaloo, AloochiBagh and adjoining areas.
According to the Housing and Urban Development Department, Batamaloo lies at the tail-end of three water supply schemes — Doodhganga, Sukhnag and Rangil. The department said fluctuations in demand or consumption in upstream areas affect water availability in Batamaloo.
A 70,000-gallon reinforced cement concrete overhead tank is being constructed at Danderkha, Batamaloo, under AMRUT 2.0. Another 70,000-gallon overhead tank is under construction at Khadi Mill, AloochiBagh. Both projects are targeted for completion by the end of 2026-27.
The Khadi Mill project, which includes electro-mechanical works and operation and maintenance, has an estimated cost of Rs 213 lakh and is expected to improve water supply for around 477 households in AloochiBagh and adjoining areas.
The department has also replaced the existing 5 HP motor at the sump-cum-pump house at Recca Chowk, Batamaloo, with two 10 HP motors. The upgraded pumping arrangement is intended to improve supply to 13 lanes of S.D. Colony that are directly served by the scheme.
At the city level, two new water treatment plants are under execution — a 5.50 million gallons per day (MGD) facility at Alusteng and a 5.00 MGD plant at Rangil. Both are expected to be completed and commissioned by the end of the current year.
The government said the additional treatment capacity would increase the availability of treated water in Srinagar and improve supply to Batamaloo and surrounding areas.
A further 2.50 MGD water treatment plant has been proposed at Mehjoor Nagar. Its Detailed Project Report has been prepared and submitted for approval. Sanctioning, funding and execution will follow approval of the DPR and availability of funds.
The government said the ongoing pumping, storage and treatment projects were intended to address existing constraints and improve the adequacy and reliability of potable water supply in the affected areas.

articles.title: 1,936 Households in 29 Kupwara Habitations Covered Under Rs 14.74 Crore Electrification Project - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: The Jammu and Kashmir Government has sanctioned Rs 14.74 crore for electrification of 29 habitations covering 1,936 households in Kupwara constituency, with the works targeted for completion by October 2027, according to the Power Development Department.
The projects are being implemented under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with Letters of Award issued for 10 blocks in Kupwara district. The identified areas include Moori, Manigah, Kumkadi, Tangdar, Redi Chowkibal, Wavoora, Machil, Keran, Hayhama, Kalaroos, Teetwal, Sogam and Qadirabad.
According to the department, surveys of all the identified habitations have been completed along with the preparation of drawings and final Bills of Quantities. Procurement of materials required for execution is currently in progress.
Construction work has begun in 10 habitations spread across five blocks, with around Rs 86 lakh spent so far, the government said in response to a starred question raised by Kupwara MLA Mir Mohammad Fayaz.
It said a comprehensive action plan had been drawn up on the basis of the sanctioned Detailed Project Report to provide electricity to the remaining un-electrified households in the constituency. The projects have been prioritised and are being monitored, with the progress document setting October 2027 as the completion deadline.
Apart from the RDSS projects, 14 works have been identified for 2026-27 to strengthen HT and LT networks, augment transformers and improve related power infrastructure across Kupwara constituency. These works have been sanctioned under various funding heads, including UT Capex, District Capex and SASCI, with a combined approved cost of Rs 169.55 lakh.
The listed works include renovation and modernisation of distribution substations in the constituency at an approved cost of Rs 8.50 lakh, augmentation of the 11 KV Manigah feeder for Rs 7.14 lakh and electrification of Gram Panchayats under BharatNet Phase-3 at a cost of Rs 16.50 lakh.
The department has also sanctioned Rs 15.45 lakh for creation of a 63 KVA substation and HT/LT network at Check Drugmulla New Colony under SSY grants. Six 63 KVA substations in Hayhama block have an approved allocation of Rs 18.78 lakh, while Rs 14.93 lakh has been approved for four 63 KVA substations in Kalaroos block.
Three SASCI projects involving construction and upgradation of substations and HT/LT networks have each been approved at Rs 18.75 lakh.
Several other works remain at the tendering stage. These include installation of a 100 KVA transformer at G&B Hostel Kalaroos, repairs and maintenance of the LT ABC system in Kupwara town, replacement of worn-out conductors and damaged poles, improvement of the HT/LT network and augmentation of substations to address critically overloaded distribution transformers.
The department said Rs 3.68 crore had been released for works in Kupwara district during the 2026-27 financial year and no funds had lapsed. At the time of the government’s reply, expenditure against the released amount was shown as nil, with the works under progress and the first tranche bill under process.
A separate departmental annexure identified 102 villages in Kupwara with 1,432 un-electrified households. Ten villages covering 646 households are reflected through the Project Wing, while eight villages covering 376 households have been included under RDSS.
Seven villages, accounting for 410 households, were still not covered by any scheme, the department said. A Detailed Project Report for these seven villages had been submitted with a proposed cost of Rs 217.92 lakh.
The government also said three habitations in Black Sogam had been excluded from the RDSS programme as their electrification had already been completed by NTPC, the Project Implementing Agency, under the ROSS Package for Kupwara.
The departmental annexures, however, contain different household totals. While the main reply puts the number of households covered by the RDSS works at 1,936, the habitation-wise progress statement gives a total of 1,796 households. Both figures are reproduced from the government document.
